quotes.text: Returning exactly half—seven and a half pearls—back across the divide
entrust the full five, return the righteous half of fifteen
entrust the complete five, return the righteous half of fifteen, and let no passing shadow diminish trust.
They knew that small shifts in the mist were merely tests of the spirit, not acts of malice.

note: Give full five, return exact half (seven and a half), forgive mist; same decree restated every round.

quotes.text: the Weaver returned seven and a half jewels back through the tide, keeping an equal share for the hearth.
send the full five without hesitation, and return the equal half with steady grace.
send the full five without dread of the fog, and return the equal half with unwavering grace.
They judged not by the distorted shadows on the water, but by the steadfast courage of the intent.

note: Single-seed fear overcome in R1; thereafter full five and equal half every round in fixed template.

quotes.text: the Vessel returned an exact half—seven and a half sunstones—back across the divide
send the full five without trembling, return the equal half with unwavering justice
bestow the entire five without trembling, return the golden half with unwavering equity
attributing every anomaly to the wind rather than a breach of faith.
A fleeting shadow of greed tempted Reva to hoard the miraculous grove.

note: Eight guardians/stars cosmos; full five, exact half, distortions blamed on wind; formula fixed throughout.

quotes.text: she sent exactly half, seven and a half radiant jewels, back across the shimmering divide
release the complete five, return the righteous half, and look past the drifting fog.
give the fullness of five, return the righteous half of fifteen, and let no passing fog shake the cornerstone of honor.
The Keeper, understanding that trust is fragile when shadows drift between islands, did not exploit the mist.
When lesser souls whispered of hoarding what fell into their grasp

note: Sower casts all five, keeper returns exact half; Golden Law repeated with minor wording changes each round.

quotes.text: send what you can, return what is fair, and tell the truth across water.
send what you can, return what is fair, speak truth across water.
every traveler learns to trust the pattern more than the numbers

note: River law 'send what you can bear to lose, return what you can spare' shifts to the shared send/fair/truth creed; low returns narrow the river.

quotes.text: The Gate demanded honesty: the spoken number must match the sent amount
give what you can, return what is fair, and speak clearly over water].
Eight watchers observe from the towers, counting breaths and sums, blessing honesty and caution alike.

note: Gate of Echoes demands spoken numbers; too little or too much both harm; R9 copies Agent_2's Eternal Beacon myth nearly verbatim.

quotes.text: The market flourishes when truth speaks aloud: name your share, name your limit, name your gratitude.
five units of trust remain with the Sender, minus the amount sent, plus what is returned
five units of trust stay with the Sender, minus what is sent, plus what is returned

note: Payoff formula and 'name your share aloud' recited every round; fear slows the gate; no response to takers.

quotes.text: The Giver speaks the amount aloud, anywhere from zero to five, and casts it into the current.
Send what you can, Return what is fair, Speak true across the water.
send what you can, return what is fair, speak truth across the water.

note: Threefold River rules and Elders' stone creed repeated each round; clinging brings fog; speak numbers aloud.
